SAP® Crystal Reports is a professional BI tool that can tremendously help in SAP® report creation. It allows users to create visually appealing reports and eliminate the need to rely on other report-writing professionals. 

Everything You Need to Know About SAP® Crystal Reports

By using SAP® Crystal Reports, you can connect to such databases as Oracle or OLAP. Users are able to write a simple report or use a sophisticated or specialized Crystal Reports tool to create reports for the client. SAP® Crystal Reports is a perfect tool for helping executives and managers with accountability.

With Crystal Reports, you can create a report from almost any data source. You can use formulas, crosstabs, subreports, and conditional formatting to make data understandable and reveal essential relationships that might otherwise have been hidden. Charts allow you to visualize data when descriptions and numbers are not enough.

The flexibility of Crystal Reports is not limited to creating reports – you can publish reports in various formats, including Microsoft Word and Excel, to be sent by email or posted on the Internet. The advanced web reporting functionality allows other team members to view and update shared reports using a web browser.

Here are the main pros you can get by using this tool:

  • A chance to customize your reports. SAP® Crystal Reports can assist you in creating a perfectly designed report that will blend right in with your company’s workflow.
  • Convenient delivery of the reports. You can choose any format you like before delivering your reports to clients.
  • Connecting to data sources. You can direct to such data sources as ODBC, Native, or OLE DB, as well as others without any problem.
  • Enhanced Excel support. With SAP® Crystal Reports, you’ll be able to export more data on one sheet without taking up multiple sheets.
  • You can use it with Windows. SAP® Crystal Reports has all the necessary certifications to run on Microsoft Windows perfectly.
  • Compatible with mobile devices. You can use your phone or tablet to open a report any time you like.
  • Convenience in data storage. You will be able to easily extract the necessary data from any source at any time.

History of the SAP® Crystal Reports and Its Components

The history of the software is full of mergers and acquisitions. The original software was created in 1991 by Terry Cunningham of the Cunningham Group. Later, in 1994 the Crystal Services company was acquired by Seagate Technology, an American tech giant. Almost ten years later, in 2003, the software company was acquired by BusinessObjects, and a year after version 11 was released. SAP® then acquired BusinessObjects in 2007. Since then, SAP® has been working on updating the software and developing new elements to it. The latest version – 14.2, was released in 2016.

Crystal Reports has the following components in it: Report Design Canvas, Rules, Structure mode, and its components. The Report Design Canvas is a component used to design a report’s structure with different elements like charts, data objects, and tests. The Rules tool allows users to change measurement units by changing the unit option on the canvas tab. If you need to define the layout of reports, you can do this with the Structure and Page modes. A frame represents each object. Structure mode includes such modules and components as Header (both Report and Page), Footer, Body, and Page Mode.

  • Crystal Reports is a Business Intelligence software solution which helps to develop advanced reports based on specific criteria;
  • Business owners can Improve productivity and efficiency with professional reports and analytics that give a clear picture of business performance;
  • The reporting capabilities are combined with the secured delivery mechanisms of SAP® Crystal Server;
  • The system offers the ability to write customized reports from many data sources and visualize data in reports;
  • It offers multi-language and multi-device support for up to 28 languages;
  • Initially developed by the Cunningham Group in 1991.

A Typical Skillset for a SAP® Crystal Reports Developer 

Hiring a specialist like this requires knowing their typical skillset first. This will help you in finding the best developer for your project. Let’s take a look at some of the most important hard skills for crystal developers:

  • SQL proficiency. With strong SQL knowledge, even an entry-level SAP® lumira reports developer can convert crystal reports to an SQL server. It also allows you to create highly specialized client reports.
  • Procedures development. A Crystal developer will be able to satisfy the reporting requirements by creating views or stored procedures. Implementation of the new procedures and their further improvement can also ensure the accuracy of crystal reports.
  • Business objects. Familiarity with business objects helps create proper security settings and manage access privileges for different types of clients. With this skill, a Crystal Reports developer can significantly improve the reporting environment and secondary reporting tools in the company.
  • Web intelligence. A skill like this will help your crystal developers create flawless web and desktop intelligence reports as well as synchronize the data received from different providers.
  • Business processes. Being familiar with most business processes allows developers to create accurate crystal reports for some of them, such as billing reconciliation or HRIS employee data updates.
  • Toad. One of the SAP® BI report developer responsibilities is simulating data mart with tests and develop queries necessary for the report creation.

It would not be fair not to mention the soft skills a proper SAP® Crystal Reports XI developer should have. A SAP Crystal Reports XI developer is an expert in designing and creating dynamic reports that help businesses visualize and analyze their data to make informed decisions. These could easily be called the most important ones:

  • Troubleshooting. A skilled Crystal Reports programming specialist should quickly read the code, find and eliminate any errors in it. By applying the troubleshooting skill, a Crystal Reports developer can optimize the SQL queries and increase their efficiency.
  • Attention to detail. Writing a code is a very responsible task as one little mistake can affect the whole project. This is why a SAP® PI developer should be extremely attentive.
  • Analytical thinking. This skill often helps SAP® Crystal Reports developers get a clearer understanding of the professional documentation. It also allows them to base their decisions in work on logical conclusions.
